source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: No early-papyrus witness preserves Matthew 6 within the 2nd-3rd c. CE corpus for these target verses; primary witnesses are the 4th c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference (where variants are documented)
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997; Luz Hermeneia 2001-2007; France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1993-1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Betz Hermeneia 1995; Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua; the SBLGNT polytonic-with-spaces is the modern critical reconstruction. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials. The Lord's-Prayer doxology variant at v.13 is one of the most famous text-critical loci in the entire New Testament.

verses.text: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: Prosechete de tēn dikaiosynēn hymōn mē poiein emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn pros to theathēnai autois· ei de mē ge, misthon ouk echete para tō patri hymōn tō en tois ouranois.
verses.notes: OPENING THESIS for the three-acts-of-piety section (vv.1-18: almsgiving, prayer, fasting). Variant: many Byzantine MSS read *eleēmosynēn* (almsgiving) instead of *dikaiosynēn* (righteousness); the latter is preferred (Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, NA28, SBLGNT). The shift to *dikaiosynē* as the umbrella-term for the three practices reflects rabbinic usage where *ṣěḏāqâ* came to denote almsgiving specifically (cf. Tob 1:3, 12:8-9). Davies-Allison ICC 1.575-579.

verses.text: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Hotan oun poiēs eleēmosynēn, mē salpisēs emprosthen sou, hōsper hoi hypokritai poiousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais rhymais, hopōs doxasthōsin hypo tōn anthrōpōn· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.
verses.notes: FIRST PIETY-ACT: ALMSGIVING. *hypokritēs* — originally a stage-actor; metaphorically a hypocrite/play-actor. The Matthean polemic against *hypokritai* targets specifically a particular type of religious self-display, not Judaism as a whole. **EDITOR FLAG**: avoid anti-Judaic translation of *hypokritai* that conflates with 'Pharisees' or 'Jews'; the term is type-specific. *apechousin ton misthon* (they have received their reward) — *apechō* in commercial context = 'receipt-in-full.' Davies-Allison ICC 1.579-583; Luz Hermeneia 1.348-355.

verses.text: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,
verses.translit: sou de poiountos eleēmosynēn mē gnōtō hē aristera sou ti poiei hē dexia sou,
verses.notes: LEFT-HAND / RIGHT-HAND hyperbole. The proverbial expression for absolute secrecy in giving. cf. b. Bava Batra 9b (rabbinic anonymous-almsgiving tradition: 'one who gives charity in secret is greater than Moses').

verses.text: ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
verses.translit: hopōs ē sou hē eleēmosynē en tō kryptō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi.
verses.notes: Variant: Byzantine MSS add *en tō phanerō* ("openly") to *apodōsei soi* — a moralizing harmonization. The earliest witnesses (Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, NA28, SBLGNT) read without the addition. The 'reward in secret' tension with public-reward is part of the verse's force.

verses.text: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Kai hotan proseuchēsthe, ouk esesthe hōs hoi hypokritai· hoti philousin en tais synagōgais kai en tais gōniais tōn plateiōn hestōtes proseuchesthai, hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.
verses.notes: SECOND PIETY-ACT: PRAYER. Variant: NA28/SBLGNT/Vaticanus read *esesthe* (you shall be) — future indicative used as imperative; some witnesses read singular *esē*.

verses.text: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
verses.translit: sy de hotan proseuchē, eiselthe eis to tameion sou kai kleisas tēn thyran sou proseuxai tō patri sou tō en tō kryptō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryptō apodōsei soi.
verses.notes: PRIVATE PRAYER. *tameion* — inner room / storeroom; in a typical 1st-c. Palestinian house, the only lockable interior space. cf. Isa 26:20 LXX. The 'Father in secret' should NOT be translated as if 'secret Father' (heretical). Davies-Allison ICC 1.586-588.

verses.text: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται.
verses.translit: Proseuchomenoi de mē battalogēsēte hōsper hoi ethnikoi, dokousin gar hoti en tē polylogia autōn eisakousthēsontai.
verses.notes: *battalogeō* — a Greek hapax legomenon, of disputed etymology: possibly onomatopoeic (bat-bat-bat) for stammering/babbling; possibly from *battos* (a stutterer in Greek proverb); possibly Semitic loan. The reference is to pagan magical-incantation prayers (cf. Acts 19:13-19; PGM corpus) reciting divine names repeatedly to compel divine response. The Matthean polemic targets manipulation of the divine via verbal repetition. Davies-Allison ICC 1.588-591.

verses.text: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
verses.translit: mē oun homoiōthēte autois, oiden gar ho patēr hymōn hōn chreian echete pro tou hymas aitēsai auton.
verses.notes: DIVINE FOREKNOWLEDGE OF NEEDS — the theological premise of the Lord's Prayer that follows. The Father's knowledge precedes the asking; prayer is therefore not informational but relational.

verses.text: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου,
verses.translit: Houtōs oun proseuchesthe hymeis· Pater hēmōn ho en tois ouranois, hagiasthētō to onoma sou,
verses.notes: LORD'S PRAYER OPENING — *Pater hēmōn ho en tois ouranois* ("Our Father who [are] in the heavens"). **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: Raël *The Role of Christ* engages 'our Father in heaven' as direct Elohim-address — literally 'our Fathers among the celestial bodies.' **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve text; do NOT pre-resolve toward (a) the Raëlian Elohim-address reading or (b) the orthodox-Christian Trinitarian-Father reading. *hagiasthētō to onoma sou* (let your name be sanctified) — divine passive; structural echo of the Kaddish prayer *yitgaddal we-yitqaddash sh'meh rabbā*. Davies-Allison ICC 1.595-602; Brown 1965 *The Pater Noster as an Eschatological Prayer*.

verses.text: ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς.
verses.translit: elthetō hē basileia sou, genēthētō to thelēma sou, hōs en ouranō kai epi gēs.
verses.notes: KINGDOM-COMING + WILL-DONE petitions. The *hōs en ouranō kai epi gēs* (as in heaven, also on earth) likely qualifies both prior petitions (sanctification of name AND coming of kingdom AND doing of will). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the Raëlian canon reads *en ouranō* (in the heavens) as 'on the home planet' — preserve text; the standard reading is the divine-realm cosmography of Jewish apocalyptic.

verses.text: Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
verses.translit: Ton arton hēmōn ton epiousion dos hēmin sēmeron·
verses.notes: DAILY BREAD — *epiousios* is one of the most famous translation cruxes in the entire NT. The word is a Greek hapax (appearing only here and in the Lukan parallel Lk 11:3). Proposed etymologies: (a) *epi + ousia* = 'for our subsistence' / 'necessary'; (b) *epi + iōn* = 'for the coming day' (tomorrow's bread); (c) *epi + ousia* in eschatological sense = 'the bread of the coming age.' Jerome's Vulgate famously rendered it *supersubstantialem* (super-substantial) — preserving the eschatological reading. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.607-610 (extensive discussion); Brown 1965.

verses.text: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: kai aphes hēmin ta opheilēmata hēmōn, hōs kai hēmeis aphēkamen tois opheiletais hēmōn·
verses.notes: FORGIVENESS PETITION. *opheilēmata* (debts) — the Matthean wording uses commercial-debt language, where the Lukan parallel (Lk 11:4) uses *hamartias* (sins) softened by debt-language. The Aramaic *ḥôbâ* covers both meanings ('debt' AND 'sin'). The reciprocal *hōs kai hēmeis aphēkamen* (as we have also forgiven) — note the aorist (past) tense in the earliest witnesses, not present tense ('as we forgive'). The forgiveness-conditional is unambiguous (cf. vv.14-15).

verses.text: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
verses.translit: kai mē eisenenkēs hēmas eis peirasmon, alla rhysai hēmas apo tou ponērou.
verses.notes: **MAJOR TEXTUAL VARIANT — THE LORD'S-PRAYER DOXOLOGY**. The famous *hoti sou estin hē basileia kai hē dynamis kai hē doxa eis tous aiōnas. amēn.* ("for thine is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever, amen") is **ABSENT** from the earliest witnesses: Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, codices D, Z, and the Vulgate. It IS present in the Byzantine majority text (the source of the Textus Receptus + KJV) and in the Didache 8:2 (early 2nd c. liturgical adaptation). NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT all omit the doxology as a later liturgical accretion. The shorter ending (ending with 'deliver us from evil/the evil one') is the Matthean original; the doxology was incorporated from Jewish doxological prayer-conventions for liturgical use. Davies-Allison ICC 1.615-617. *eis peirasmon* (into trial/temptation) — *peirasmos* refers to eschatological testing-of-faith (cf. Mt 26:41; Rev 3:10), not generic moral temptation. *tou ponērou* — masculine 'the evil one' (= Satan) or neuter 'evil' — same ambiguity as Mt 5:37, 13:19, 13:38.

verses.text: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
verses.translit: ean gar aphēte tois anthrōpois ta paraptōmata autōn, aphēsei kai hymin ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios·
verses.notes: POST-PRAYER COMMENTARY on the forgiveness petition. *paraptōmata* (trespasses, falls) — different word from v.12's *opheilēmata*, indicating the petition's substance shifts as it is explicated. The conditional is strongly reciprocal-causal: divine forgiveness is conditioned on human forgiveness.

verses.text: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: ean de mē aphēte tois anthrōpois, oude ho patēr hymōn aphēsei ta paraptōmata hymōn.
verses.notes: The negative form of v.14. Variant: some witnesses (Vaticanus, NA28, SBLGNT) read shorter form without *ta paraptōmata autōn* after *tois anthrōpois*; some add. The shorter reading is preferred.

verses.text: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Hotan de nēsteuēte, mē ginesthe hōs hoi hypokritai skythrōpoi, aphanizousin gar ta prosōpa autōn hopōs phanōsin tois anthrōpois nēsteuontes· amēn legō hymin, apechousin ton misthon autōn.
verses.notes: THIRD PIETY-ACT: FASTING. *skythrōpoi* (sullen-faced); *aphanizousin* (disfigure/make unsightly) — wordplay with *phanōsin* (be seen): they DIS-figure to be SEEN. Pious 1st-c. Jewish fasting included unkempt appearance / ashes-on-head; the polemic targets the performative form.

verses.text: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,
verses.translit: sy de nēsteuōn aleipsai sou tēn kephalēn kai to prosōpon sou nipsai,
verses.notes: ANOINT-AND-WASH instruction. Anointing-with-oil + face-washing were normal grooming for non-fast days; the instruction is to fast secretly, looking unfasting in public.

verses.text: ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
verses.translit: hopōs mē phanēs tois anthrōpois nēsteuōn alla tō patri sou tō en tō kryphaiō· kai ho patēr sou ho blepōn en tō kryphaiō apodōsei soi.
verses.notes: Structural close of the three-piety section. Note that *kryphaiō* (here) and *kryptō* (vv.4, 6) both translate the same Semitic concept; the variation may be Matthean stylistic. Davies-Allison ICC 1.620.

verses.text: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
verses.translit: Mē thēsaurizete hymin thēsaurous epi tēs gēs, hopou sēs kai brōsis aphanizei, kai hopou kleptai dioryssousin kai kleptousin·
verses.notes: TREASURE-IN-HEAVEN section opens. *sēs* (moth) + *brōsis* (literally 'eating' — moth, rust, corrosion); *dioryssō* (dig through) — Palestinian houses were mud-brick; thieves literally dug through walls. cf. Job 4:19; Sir 29:8-13; cf. Mt 19:21 (the rich young ruler).

verses.text: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
verses.translit: thēsaurizete de hymin thēsaurous en ouranō, hopou oute sēs oute brōsis aphanizei, kai hopou kleptai ou dioryssousin oude kleptousin·
verses.notes: POSITIVE COUNTERPART. *thēsaurous en ouranō* — eschatological merit-deposit. cf. Tob 4:9; Sir 29:11; m. Pe'ah 1:1 (rabbinic merit-deposit-in-heaven concept); 2 Bar 14:12; Pirke Avot 2:1.

verses.text: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.
verses.translit: hopou gar estin ho thēsauros sou, ekei estai kai hē kardia sou.
verses.notes: Heart-follows-treasure proverb. Note the second-person singular (*sou*) — direct address. Variant: Lukan parallel (Lk 12:34) reads plural; the Matthean singular is more proverbial.

verses.text: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
verses.translit: Ho lychnos tou sōmatos estin ho ophthalmos. ean oun ē ho ophthalmos sou haplous, holon to sōma sou phōteinon estai·
verses.notes: EYE-AS-LAMP. *haplous* (single, sincere, generous) — has a moral connotation in Jewish-Hellenistic usage of generosity / single-mindedness (cf. Test. Iss. 3:4; LXX 1 Chr 29:17). The ancient physiology of vision: eye as window through which light enters/exits the body. The verse plays on this. Davies-Allison ICC 1.635-641; Betz 1995.

verses.text: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
verses.translit: ean de ho ophthalmos sou ponēros ē, holon to sōma sou skoteinon estai. ei oun to phōs to en soi skotos estin, to skotos poson.
verses.notes: *ophthalmos ponēros* (evil eye) — Semitic idiom for stinginess / envious-look (cf. Prov 23:6; 28:22 LXX; Mt 20:15; m. Avot 2:9). The eye-as-lamp + 'evil eye' = stingy giving. The verse fits the surrounding generosity-motif. Davies-Allison ICC 1.640.

verses.text: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
verses.translit: Oudeis dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein· ē gar ton hena misēsei kai ton heteron agapēsei, ē henos anthexetai kai tou heterou kataphronēsei. ou dynasthe theō douleuein kai mamōna.
verses.notes: TWO-MASTERS PROVERB. *mamōnas* — Aramaic loanword (*māmōnāʾ* = wealth, property; cognate to Hebrew *mātmôn* = treasure). Preserved untranslated (cf. Lk 16:9, 11, 13) — likely retained from the early Aramaic Jesus-tradition. Cross-corpus: cf. Q-source parallel Lk 16:13; cf. CD 4:17 (Qumran on wealth as Belial's snare); cf. Sir 31:5-11.

verses.text: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε ἢ τί πίητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
verses.translit: Dia touto legō hymin· mē merimnate tē psychē hymōn ti phagēte ē ti piēte, mēde tō sōmati hymōn ti endysēsthe· ouchi hē psychē pleion estin tēs trophēs kai to sōma tou endymatos?
verses.notes: ANXIETY-DISCOURSE BEGINS. *merimnaō* (be anxious / take thought) — the keyword of vv.25-34. Variant: Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + NA28/SBLGNT include *ē ti piēte* (or what you shall drink); some witnesses omit, likely homoioteleuton. Cross-corpus: cf. Stoic discourse on *merimna* (Epictetus, Seneca); cf. Cynic peripatetic-poverty ethics.

verses.text: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
verses.translit: emblepsate eis ta peteina tou ouranou hoti ou speirousin oude therizousin oude synagousin eis apothēkas, kai ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios trephei auta· ouch hymeis mallon diapherete autōn?
verses.notes: BIRDS-OF-THE-AIR illustration. *qal vāḥōmer* (a-fortiori) argument from lesser to greater — standard rabbinic argumentation. cf. Job 38:41; Ps 147:9; Ps Sol 5:9-11.

verses.text: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
verses.translit: tis de ex hymōn merimnōn dynatai prostheinai epi tēn hēlikian autou pēchyn hena?
verses.notes: *hēlikia* — ambiguous: 'stature/height' or 'lifespan/age.' *pēchys* — cubit (~45 cm). 'Add a cubit to your height' would be absurdly large; 'add a moment to your lifespan' (with *pēchys* as time-metaphor) reads more naturally — though 'add a cubit to your height' as deliberately-absurd hyperbole is also defensible. Davies-Allison ICC 1.652-654.

verses.text: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·
verses.translit: kai peri endymatos ti merimnate? katamathete ta krina tou agrou pōs auxanousin· ou kopiōsin oude nēthousin·
verses.notes: LILIES-OF-THE-FIELD. *krina* — likely a generic 'wildflowers' rather than specifically lilies (Lilium spp.); possibly anemones (Anemone coronaria) which are common spring wildflowers in Galilee. Variant: Vaticanus + Sinaiticus(corrected) read *auxanousin ou kopiōsin oude nēthousin*; original Sinaiticus reads *ou xenousin oude nēthousin* (a unique reading).

verses.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
verses.translit: legō de hymin hoti oude Solomōn en pasē tē doxē autou periebaleto hōs hen toutōn.
verses.notes: SOLOMON COMPARISON. *en pasē tē doxē* — Solomon's legendary regal-finery (1 Kgs 10; 2 Chr 9). Even Solomon's wardrobe inferior to wildflower-beauty — the *qal vāḥōmer* extension.

verses.text: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
verses.translit: ei de ton chorton tou agrou sēmeron onta kai aurion eis klibanon ballomenon ho theos houtōs amphiennysin, ou pollō mallon hymas, oligopistoi?
verses.notes: *oligopistoi* — uniquely Matthean address (8:26; 14:31; 16:8; cf. Lk 12:28). 'Little-faiths.' Wild grass burned in clay ovens (*klibanos*) as fuel — the ephemeral plant clothed splendidly by God for one day yields the lesser/greater argument.

verses.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
verses.translit: mē oun merimnēsēte legontes· Ti phagōmen? ē· Ti piōmen? ē· Ti peribalōmetha?
verses.notes: The three anxious-questions restatement — food, drink, clothing — the basic-needs triad.

verses.text: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
verses.translit: panta gar tauta ta ethnē epizētousin· oiden gar ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios hoti chrēzete toutōn hapantōn.
verses.notes: *ta ethnē* — the nations / Gentiles. Pejorative Matthean-community marker (cf. Mt 5:47). Echoes v.8: divine fore-knowledge of need.

verses.text: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: zēteite de prōton tēn basileian kai tēn dikaiosynēn autou, kai tauta panta prostethēsetai hymin.
verses.notes: Variant: many Byzantine MSS read *tēn basileian tou theou* (kingdom of God); Vaticanus reads simply *tēn basileian* (the kingdom); NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT prefer the shorter Vaticanus reading. Sinaiticus reads *tēn basileian tōn ouranōn*. The *autou* (his) refers to God (the heavenly Father from v.32).

verses.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ἑαυτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: mē oun merimnēsēte eis tēn aurion, hē gar aurion merimnēsei heautēs· arketon tē hēmera hē kakia autēs.
verses.notes: PROVERBIAL CLOSE — 'sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof' (KJV). The personified *aurion* (tomorrow) takes care of its own anxieties. *kakia* here = 'trouble/affliction' not moral evil. Cross-corpus: cf. b. Sanhedrin 100b (rabbinic 'do not worry about tomorrow's troubles'); cf. Stoic *prosochē tou parontos* (attention to the present).
